voice-unicode-crash.evidence: content/quantum-observable-universe/mass-endomorphism/binding-qbeta-complex-volume.md:148: uncertainty of $\pm 1.26$ (130× / 32× the value); only the swing

FALSE POSITIVE, checked against the repo's own crash list. The criterion flagged 'x' U+00D7 MULTIPLICATION SIGN in prose at line 148 ('130x / 32x the value'), outside any $...$, at severity CRITICAL. U+00D7 is NOT in NO_LATEX_SETUP in folio-assistant/content/pipeline/render-latex.ts — the 42-character set that aborts pdflatex, derived EMPIRICALLY by emitting every distinct non-ASCII char in the corpus against the real preamble and collecting what pdflatex rejects. That list contains the two chars AGENTS.md names as crash-class (U+02E3 MODIFIER LETTER SMALL X, U+2207 NABLA) and does not contain U+00D7, which utf8.def declares as \texttimes. This is AGENTS.md's own rule — '"Unmapped" != "crashes"' — and the criterion is not applying it.
voice-unicode-crash.notes: Two cautions for whoever tunes this criterion. (1) It reports ONE occurrence per run, so clearing a flagged char just surfaces the next and reads like the fix did not work. (2) It nearly cost two unnecessary edits here: it first flagged 'zeta-4' (U+03B6 + U+2084) in a section header, and NEITHER of those is in the crash list either. That text was still changed to $\zeta_4$ — but as NOTATION CONSISTENCY (line 118 of the same file already wrote $\zeta_4$, and the repo's TeX conventions put math in math mode), NOT as a crash fix. It should not be cited as one. The remaining non-ASCII in this file is x, en-dash and em-dash, all declared. Note also that VERBATIM_TRANSLIT does NOT rescue prose: it applies to verbatim and inline-code contexts only, so 'the renderer transliterates it' is not a valid safety argument for prose -- NO_LATEX_SETUP is.
